question_stem:
A ball is fired horizontally with a speed of $41.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ from a stationary cannon at the top of a hill. The ball lands on horizontal ground that is a vertical distance of $57\text{ m}$ below the cannon, as shown in Fig. 3.1.
{{figure:figure_3_1}}
Fig. 3.1 (not to scale)
Assume air resistance is negligible.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Show that the time taken for the ball to reach the ground, after being fired, is $3.4\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Calculate the horizontal distance of the ball from the cannon at the point where the ball lands on the ground.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Determine the magnitude of the displacement of the ball from the cannon at the point where the ball lands on the ground.

parts.label: (d)
parts.part_stem: The ball leaves the cannon at time $t = 0$.

parts.label: (e)
parts.part_stem: The cannon recoils horizontally with a speed of $0.340\text{ m s}^{-1}$ when it fires the ball. The total mass of the ball and the cannon is $1480\text{ kg}$. Assume that no external horizontal forces act on the ball-cannon system.
parts.text: Determine, to three significant figures, the mass of the ball.

parts.label: (f)
parts.part_stem: The cannon now fires a ball of smaller mass. Assume that air resistance is still negligible.
parts.text: State and explain the change, if any, to the graph in Fig. 3.2 due to the decreased mass of the ball.
